title: Closed food chain in condensates (fuel -> prey droplets -> predator droplets -> waste -> fuel): from full-domain noise, predator droplets nucleate on prey droplets, eat them at the contact and spread as an expanding predation front that leaves a fuel-rich clearing, which prey droplets then recolonize; predators go extinct after one wave (2/2 seeds at 256^2)
summary: Two immiscible autocatalytic Cahn-Hilliard condensates share one closed mass budget: prey material grows from a diffusing fuel, predator material grows by mass action from prey material, and both decay to a waste that regrows into fuel everywhere; no term refers to a body, a distance or a kind, so predation is a reaction between two materials. From smoothed noise over the whole domain (seed 0, pack/sheet.png), ~200 prey droplets form, predator caps sit on prey droplets and eat them from one side (bitten crescents), and the predators organise into a ring that expands through the emulsion for ~3000 t, leaving an empty high-fuel zone that prey refill as large worm-shaped droplets from t~3500. The predators then thin out and are gone by t~8000 (seed 0); on seed 1 (seed1_screen.png, same parameters) they die by t~2000, and at 128^2 the same world is all-or-nothing (predators either eat every prey by k2>=0.2 or starve by k2<=0.15), so persistence is not yet established. Total mass drifts ~2% only through the clipped reporting of c; predator droplet births and the prey's own division are not yet measured.
